title: Streams decide the best Afrobeats artist (formal English)
proposition: Streaming numbers alone are the best way to decide who the best Afrobeats artist is.
rationale: AGAINST explains concretely why streams measure reach, not quality (marketing, playlists, uncounted listening in Nigeria, manipulation, longevity and influence) and rebuts 'awards are political'; FOR repeats 'numbers don't lie' without engaging. The word 'alone' makes FOR's burden heavy.

opening.text:
Numbers do not lie. The artist with the most streams on Spotify, Apple Music and Audiomack is the artist the most people choose to listen to, and that is the fairest way to decide who is best.

Everything else is opinion. Awards are political and decided by small committees, critics have their favourites, and fan bases shout the loudest on social media. Streams are the only measure where every listener counts.

rebuttal.text: Complaints about bought streams are excuses from fans whose favourite artist is losing. Listeners vote with their data, and the numbers are what they are.

opening.text:
Streams measure how many plays a song gets on certain platforms. That is a measure of reach, not of who is the best artist, and using it alone is misleading for four reasons.

First, streams follow money and placement. Playlist slots, label marketing budgets and one viral TikTok moment can multiply plays without saying anything about songwriting or performance.

Second, a lot of listening in Nigeria is not counted. Many people hear music on the radio, in clubs, at parties, on YouTube, or through downloaded files shared between phones. A metric that misses much of the home audience cannot crown the best artist from that home.

Third, streams can be manipulated. Platforms regularly remove artificial streams generated by bots and streaming farms.

Fourth, 'best' includes things streams cannot see: live performance, longevity, influence on other musicians and the quality of a whole catalogue. Fela Kuti created Afrobeat and his influence is unmatched, yet he recorded almost entirely before streaming existed.

rebuttal.text: My opponent says awards are political. Even if that is true, it does not make streams neutral; streams are shaped by marketing money and playlist decisions too. A measure that would rank a single viral song above a fifteen-year catalogue is measuring hype, not artistry. I have not argued that streams are useless, only that they cannot be the only measure, which is what the proposition claims.
